purpose: Composition primitives for building accessible, pixel-perfect data tables, in two modes. **Composition mode** (default): compose the anatomy by hand (header / body / rows / cells) — the component owns markup, tokens, a11y, configurable column sizing (an emphasized first column), sortable headers, selectable rows, and a **freeze system** for sticky columns (e.g. an actions column) and a sticky header. **Data-driven mode**: pass `data` + `columns` and the table renders itself via the headless **`@tanstack/vue-table`** engine, still rendering through the same primitives (our markup/tokens/a11y, pixel-perfect to Figma). Pairs with the [`Pagination`](./pagination.md) component (rendered automatically in the footer when `paginated`). A top **toolbar band** (`title` / `toolbar` / `filters` slots) sits above the scroll viewport in both modes for a title, search / filter / export / column-selector actions, and removable filter chips; the `toolbar` and `filters` slots are scoped with the TanStack `table` instance (in data-driven mode) so the consumer can drive filtering, global search, and column visibility through the table's own methods. **Engine.** Data-driven mode is driven by **`@tanstack/vue-table`** (`useVueTable` + `getCoreRowModel` / `getSortedRowModel` / `getFilteredRowModel` / `getPaginationRowModel`), covering sorting, pagination, row selection, column visibility, and global filtering — client- and server-side (`manualSorting` / `manualPagination` / `manualFiltering`). It is a pure-logic library (no markup/styles/positioning/animation), granted narrowly to this single component per [`.claude/rules/dependencies.md`](../.claude/rules/dependencies.md) § Exceptions; rendering stays 100% in our primitives. State is exposed via v-model (`sorting`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility`, `globalFilter`, `pagination`, plus the structured `filters` model and the aggregate `state` snapshot below). `@tanstack/virtual` remains forbidden: the opt-in `virtual` mode windows the rows itself (spacer padding above and below the rendered slice, sized from a height index: each rendered row is measured with a `ResizeObserver`, rows not yet rendered take the average of the first rows measured, and when a row above the rows in view changes height the scroll position moves by the same amount so the rows in view stay still). Without `virtual`, a list of more than 200 rows renders its first 50 rows and mounts the rest as a spacer below them nears the viewport (an `IntersectionObserver`), so a long page costs what is on screen. **Toolbar & imperative API.** The toolbar band composes context-aware controls that drive the table through the injected context with no wiring: `Table.Filter` (a structured field/operator/value builder that commits removable/editable filter chips, with an escape slot to plug a custom builder such as the console's AQL), `Table.AppliedFilters` (the chips), `Table.ColumnSelector` (a column-visibility picker over the existing `columnVisibility` state), `Table.Export` (CSV download), and `Table.RefreshButton`. Structured filters are a first-class model (`v-model:filters`, an `AppliedFilter[]` distinct from the free-text `globalFilter`) mapped to the TanStack column filters client-side, or emitted for a server refetch under `manualFiltering`. A `loading` prop renders skeleton rows for dynamic (server-side) data. The root exposes a **curated imperative API** via `defineExpose` (`reload`, `clearFilters`, `exportCsv`, `getState`, `setState`) so controls or logic outside the table can drive it through a template ref, and a serializable `TableStateSnapshot` (`sorting` / `pagination` / `columnVisibility` / `columnOrder` / `globalFilter` / `filters`) is exposed via `v-model:state` + `getState()` / `setState()` + an `initialState` seed — the component stays router-agnostic, so the consuming app owns any URL / localStorage persistence. CSV serialization lives in a pure util at [`@aziontech/webkit/utils/csv`](../packages/webkit/src/utils/csv.ts) (`toCsv` + `downloadCsv`). **Types** (declared in `injection-key.ts`, re-exported for consumers): `FilterOperator` = `'eq' | 'neq' | 'contains' | 'not-contains' | 'starts-with' | 'ends-with' | 'gt' | 'gte' | 'lt' | 'lte' | 'in' | 'not-in' | 'is-empty' | 'is-not-empty'`; `FilterField` = `{ id: string; label: string; type: 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'multi-select' | 'boolean' | 'date'; operators?: FilterOperator[]; options?: { label: string; value: string | number | boolean }[] }`; `AppliedFilter` = `{ field: string; operator: FilterOperator; value: string | number | boolean | Array<string | number>; label?: string }`; `TableStateSnapshot` = `{ sorting?: SortingState; pagination?: PaginationState; columnVisibility?: VisibilityState; columnOrder?: string[]; globalFilter?: string; filters?: AppliedFilter[] }` (every field optional so `setState` / `initialState` accept a partial; JSON-serializable). **Collections.** `useCollection` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-collection`) drives the data-driven mode in both client and server modes: `tableProps` binds `data` (one page), `columns` (ordered by the saved preferences), `rowKey`, `loading`, `sorting`, `manualSorting` / `manualFiltering` / `manualPagination`, `paginated`, `pagination`, `rowCount`, `rowsPerPageOptions`, `enableRowSelection`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility` and the three display preferences (`density`, `wrapLines`, `striped`) together with their update handlers, and `exportRows`, in one `v-bind`. The table keeps rendering one page; the composable owns filtering, sorting, paging and selection across pages, so `exportRows` hands `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` every match rather than the page: in client mode the matching items (or every item for the `all` scope), in server mode what the collection's `exportAll` callback loads (the loaded page when there is none). **Cell presets and reordering.** Six presets render the cells every list repeats, each inside a `#cell-<id>` slot: `Table.CellLink` (a name that leaves the screen: an optional muted leading glyph (`icon`) for the provider or resource type, a 12 px external mark, a tooltip naming the destination, underline on hover, no mark without a destination; optional `+N` overflow through `OverflowCount` and a copy button pinned to the end edge), `Table.CellId` (an identifier with its copy button), `Table.CellStatus` (one semantic `Tag`), `Table.CellTags` (as many tags as fit, the rest behind `+N`), `Table.CellTime` (avatar of the author plus a relative time that updates every minute, or counts from the nearest `WebkitProvider`'s `now`, the absolute time on the tooltip and for screen readers) and `Table.CellActions` (the row menu named after the row). `reorderable` adds a leading grip column: drag a grip with the pointer, or focus it and press Arrow Up, Arrow Down, Home or End; the table emits `update:data` with the reordered records and `reorder` with `{ from, to, row }`, announces every move in a polite status region and locks while a sort is applied; `rowReorderable` keeps chosen rows (a pinned default) in place.
useWhen: Records with the same fields shown in rows and columns, where the reader compares, sorts, selects or acts on rows (resource lists, logs, usage breakdowns).
A list needs a toolbar for search, structured filters, column visibility, CSV export or refresh — the `Table.*` toolbar parts drive the table through context.
Server-backed data that pages, sorts or filters on the API: `manual-pagination`, `manual-sorting` and `manual-filtering` emit the state instead of slicing locally.
avoidWhen: A short titled preview of a longer listing on a marketing page → use `listing-table`.
A feature-by-feature comparison of Azion with a competitor → use `comparison-table`.
Rows of mixed content (media, title, description, actions) that do not share columns → use `item`.
A grid of selectable cards or options → use `radio-cards`.
related: pagination` — the page strip; a data-driven table with `paginated` renders and wires it in the footer.
listing-table` — marketing section that composes `table` for a linked preview of a list.
empty-state` — the pattern behind the table's default `empty` slot; override the slot for resource-specific copy and actions.
item` — list rows without a column structure.
bestPractices: For repeated data, use data-driven mode: pass `data` + `columns` (any non-empty `columns` switches it on) and customize cells with the `cell-<columnId>` / `header-<columnId>` slots instead of composing N rows by hand. Compose `Table.Header` / `Table.Body` / `Table.Row` / `Table.Cell` only for small, static tables.
Give rows a stable id under `row-key` (default `'id'`); selection and `v-model:row-selection` are keyed by it.
Mark the row-actions column `kind: 'action'` so it pins to the trailing edge; give chip or short-token columns a `minWidth` rather than a fixed `width`.

Give `Table.CellTime` dates from your data. Where the text must not depend on when it renders (an example, a test, a server render the browser hydrates), set `now` on the app's `WebkitProvider` and count sample dates back from that constant; never build them from `Date.now()` / `new Date()` in setup.
Drive loading through the `loading` prop (skeleton rows, `aria-busy`) and keep the `empty` slot for no-data copy — do not swap the table for a spinner.

On a phone a console list keeps its grid and scrolls sideways (the default). Set `stackable` only for a short list read one record at a time on a narrow, phone-first surface (a marketing listing, a summary in a side panel), where a card per row reads better than a scroll; never on a resource index, a log or a list compared across columns.

Place `Table.Search`, `Table.Filter`, `Table.ColumnSelector`, `Table.Export` and `Table.RefreshButton` in the `toolbar` slot with no `v-model` wiring — they read the table from context. `Table.Search` and `Table.ColumnSelector` act on the TanStack instance, so they need data-driven mode.
